project.title: English Polite Requests: Can, Could and May
project.target_audience: Japanese-speaking learners of English at beginner to intermediate level

visual_style.font_mood: Modern, highly legible sans-serif; support Japanese CJK glyphs and Latin English phrases
consistency_rules: Use green for CAN/casual, blue for COULD/polite, and purple for MAY/formal.
Keep all educational objects and text in the upper 76 percent of the frame.
Reserve the bottom 24 percent of the frame for app-generated karaoke subtitles.
Use one primary learning point per scene.
Every scene is renderable without external media using visual_fallback.

learning_analysis.topic: Choosing polite English request forms: Can, Could and May
learning_analysis.audience_level: Beginner to intermediate English learners who understand Japanese narration
learning_objectives: Recognize the relative level of formality associated with Can, Could and May in the examples in this lesson.
Choose Can for casual and familiar interactions, Could for softer and more polite requests, and May for formal contexts as presented in the script.
Understand that tone, please and a friendly expression also affect how a request sounds.
Apply Could when asking a boss for Friday off in the quiz example.

key_concepts.name: Can
key_concepts.explanation: Casual and friendly; used with friends, family and people the speaker knows well.

key_concepts.name: Could
key_concepts.explanation: Softer and more polite; suitable for colleagues, teachers, shop staff and people who are not very close.

key_concepts.name: May
key_concepts.explanation: The most formal option in this lesson, associated with hotels, offices and email.

key_concepts.name: Tone and politeness
key_concepts.explanation: Tone is as important as wording; please and a smile can make Can sound warm and friendly.

key_concepts.name: Choosing a request for a boss
key_concepts.explanation: The lesson's quiz recommends “Could I take Friday off, please?” as the more natural-sounding option in the scenario.

relationships.relation: modifies how a request is perceived alongside

learning_analysis.summary: The lesson presents Can, Could and May as a progression from casual to more formal requests. It also emphasizes that tone, please and a smile affect how polite a request sounds, and recommends Could in the example of asking a boss for Friday off.
uncertainties: The transcript's politeness scale is presented as a teaching simplification; the storyboard preserves the script's framing and does not add additional grammar caveats.

source_segments.text: このシーンを想像してみて。カフェにいて、すごく喉が渇いて「水、くれる？」って言うんだ。言葉は正しいけど、ちょっとぶっきらぼうに聞こえる。なぜかって？英語には丁寧に聞くための特別な表現があって、相手によって使い分けるんだ。
まずは can から。カジュアルでフレンドリー。友達や家族、よく知っている相手に使う。
Can you pass the salt?
Can I borrow your pen?
次は could にステップアップ。ちょっと柔らかくて丁寧。
同僚や先生、店員さん、あまり親しくない人に使える。
Could I have some water, please?
Could you help me with this?
そして最上位が may。フォーマルな場面で使う。
ホテルやオフィス、メールでよく聞く。
May I come in?
May I ask a question?
だからこれを階段みたいに考えてみて。
Can は下の段、普通。
Could は中間の段、丁寧。
May は上の段、すごくフォーマル。
小さなコツだよ。
迷ったら could を選べばほぼどこでも通用するし、いつも礼儀正しく聞こえる。
もうひとつ大事なこと。
トーンも言葉と同じくらい重要。please と笑顔を添えれば、たとえ can でも温かくフレンドリーに聞こえる。
さあ、耳をチェックしよう。
上司が通りかかって金曜に休みが欲しいとき。
「Can I have Friday off?」とか言うか、
「Could I take Friday off, please?」とか言うか。
二番目を選べば、ネイティブらしい自然な表現になる。
もっとこんなフレーズが知りたい？
Follow along.
